issues.claim: Cited in explanation, ru and en, for: "In .NET 8-10 Razor component endpoints require token validation by default. If `UseAntiforgery` is missing from the pipeline, a POST to such an endpoint fails with an exception: the endpoint has antiforgery metadata, but no middleware that supports antiforgery was found." The link title is "... (.NET 10)".
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt for the URL pinned with ?view=aspnetcore-10.0 still shows .NET 11 content: automatic CSRF middleware, Razor Components endpoints that no longer validate tokens, and a "Migrate from .NET 10 to .NET 11" link. It does not show the .NET 8-10 behaviour, the missing-middleware exception, or the placement of UseAntiforgery after UseAuthentication/UseAuthorization. The excerpt therefore does not support the claim it is cited for, and the "(.NET 10)" title does not match what was fetched. This matches my own recollection of .NET 8-10, but the cited page does not demonstrate it.
issues.suggestedFix: Cite a page whose fetched text shows the .NET 10 behaviour, for example the Blazor forms page pinned to ?view=aspnetcore-10.0 (antiforgery section) or the .NET 10 Antiforgery in ASP.NET Core page. Fetch it and check that it covers UseAntiforgery and its placement. Otherwise drop the "(.NET 10)" suffix from linkTitles and describe the exception more generally.

issues.claim: `EditForm` adds the hidden antiforgery token field to the form by itself. A manual `<AntiforgeryToken />` is needed for a plain HTML `<form>` element. / `Enhance` only replaces the full page reload with a `fetch` request and a DOM update.
issues.problem: Neither fetched excerpt shows these claims. The forms excerpt stops before the antiforgery section and before any mention of `EditForm.Enhance`. The only things it shows are a plain `<form>` with a manual `<AntiforgeryToken />` and a general note on enhanced form handling. I know both claims from the .NET 8-10 docs, but they should rest on a fetched passage. The forms link is also unpinned, and its fetched text is marked as not the latest and no longer supported.
issues.suggestedFix: Pin the forms link to ?view=aspnetcore-10.0 and confirm that the fetched text has the "EditForm adds the antiforgery token automatically" statement and the `Enhance` parameter. If it does not, add a link to the page that states them, or remove the specific claims. Apply the same check to ru options e and f.
